composio.note: Managed OAuth needs no HubSpot app of your own; Composio's docs do not say whether its managed HubSpot app is Marketplace-listed, so don't assume it escapes the 25-install cap (see uncertain). Bring your own app when you want your name on the HubSpot install screen, a different required/optional scope set (Composio's docs say not to change the managed app's default scopes; e.g. sensitive-data scopes or custom objects), your own per-account 110 req/10 s budget, or polling faster than Composio's 15-minute managed minimum. Plan for the cost: your own app is capped at 25 installs until it is listed on the HubSpot Marketplace.

verdict.headline: Build an OAuth app with distribution 'marketplace' via the HubSpot CLI; it works immediately for up to 25 customer accounts, and you need a Marketplace listing (3 active installs + initial review within 10 business days; the whole feedback process should take no more than 60 days from when feedback is shared) to go beyond that.
verdict.summary: There is no scope review. Any OAuth app can be installed by a Super Admin (or user with Marketplace Access) right away. The catch since September 2025 is install caps on the new Developer Platform: marketplace-distribution apps are capped at 25 installs until listed, private-distribution OAuth apps at 10 allowlisted accounts (100 for Solutions Partners), and static-token apps at 1. Apps are now created as CLI projects (app-hsmeta.json) rather than in a web form. Access tokens last 30 minutes, and the v1 OAuth token API is deprecated on 16 Feb 2027.
verdict.time_to_production: Same day for up to 25 accounts; uncapped after Marketplace listing: about 3-10 weeks (time to 3 active installs + up to 10 business days initial review + feedback rounds, which HubSpot says should finish within 60 days)
verdict.hands_on_effort: 2-3 hours for app + Composio + testing; 1-2 days for listing content, setup docs and shared-data table (estimates)
verdict.approval_wait: None for the first 25 installs. Marketplace listing review: initial review up to 10 business days, full feedback process should take no more than 60 days after feedback is shared; one app in review at a time.
verdict.cost: Free (developer account and test accounts); no listing fee mentioned

phases.name: Set up developer tooling
phases.goal: HubSpot CLI authenticated against your developer account, with a test account.

steps.title: Install and authenticate the HubSpot CLI
steps.detail: npm install -g @hubspot/cli@latest (v7.6.0+ required), then hs account auth, which opens a browser login to your HubSpot developer account.
steps.agent_help: Agent can install the CLI and run hs account auth; you complete the browser login.

steps.title: Create a developer test account
steps.detail: Development > Test accounts > create. Developer test accounts don't count toward the 25-install (or 10 private) cap. Until you sign the Acceptable Use Policy in the app's distribution settings, the app can only be installed in developer test accounts.

phases.name: Create the OAuth app project
phases.goal: A deployed app with OAuth auth, marketplace distribution, scopes and Composio's redirect URL.

steps.title: Choose distribution and auth type
steps.detail: For a multi-customer agent choose auth type 'oauth' with distribution 'marketplace' (Marketplace-eligible; 25 installs before listing). 'private' + oauth limits you to 10 allowlisted accounts (100 if built in a Solutions Partner portal). 'static' is a single account only and has no user-level access. Legacy private/public apps still work, but new or migrated apps follow these caps.
steps.agent_help: Agent recommends the combination from your expected customer count.

steps.title: Scaffold and write app-hsmeta.json
steps.detail: Run hs project create (App, OAuth, marketplace). In app-hsmeta.json set config.distribution='marketplace', auth.type='oauth', auth.redirectUrls (HTTPS; http only for localhost), requiredScopes (at least one; installer must grant all), optionalScopes (dropped if the account lacks them) and conditionallyRequiredScopes.
steps.agent_help: Agent can generate app-hsmeta.json with the CRM scopes below and the Composio callback in redirectUrls.

steps.title: Upload the project
steps.detail: hs project upload builds and deploys the app to your developer account.
steps.agent_help: Agent runs hs project upload once the CLI is authenticated and fixes build errors.

phases.name: Connect to Composio
phases.goal: Composio installs your HubSpot app instead of its managed one.

steps.title: Copy client ID and secret
steps.detail: hs project open > your app under Project Components > Auth tab > Client credentials.
steps.agent_help: Agent can run hs project open to take you to the right page.

steps.title: Create a custom auth config and match the redirect URL
steps.detail: Composio dashboard > Auth Configs > Create Auth Config > HubSpot > OAuth2; paste credentials; use auth_configs={"hubspot": "ac_..."}. The redirectUrls in app-hsmeta.json must contain the exact URI Composio shows, normally https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback, though some toolkits default to legacy https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add. Re-upload the project after changing it.
steps.agent_help: Agent writes session code, updates redirectUrls and re-uploads; you paste the secret.

phases.name: Test
phases.goal: Your test account connects; token refresh is robust.

steps.title: Install in the test account
steps.detail: Projects > app > Distribution tab > Add test install(s) > Install, tick the box to authorize the unverified app, then Connect app. Or run the Composio connect flow. Installers must be Super Admins or have Marketplace Access permission.
steps.agent_help: Agent generates the Composio connect link and then lists contacts to verify.

steps.title: Harden token refresh
steps.detail: Access tokens last 30 minutes (expires_in 1800). Refresh at POST https://api.hubspot.com/oauth/2026-09/token with grant_type=refresh_token. Use a distributed lock so parallel workers don't refresh at once. Migrate any v1 /oauth/v1/token usage before 16 Feb 2027.
steps.agent_help: Agent can implement or verify lock-guarded refresh and the dated token endpoint.

phases.name: Launch and Marketplace listing
phases.goal: Serve customers now (≤25), then list to remove the cap.
phases.duration: Same day for ≤25 installs; weeks to list

steps.title: Go live for up to 25 customer accounts
steps.detail: A marketplace-distribution app installs in up to 25 accounts (excluding developer test accounts) before listing, enforced since 22 Sep 2025 for 2025.2+ or migrated apps.
steps.agent_help: Agent can add an install counter/alert so you know when you're approaching 25.

steps.title: Meet listing requirements and submit
steps.detail: At least 3 active, unique, unaffiliated installs with activity in the past 30 days; OAuth as sole auth method; use every requested scope and reflect them in the Shared data table; live Terms of Service and Privacy Policy URLs; a support contact; public setup documentation for the HubSpot integration. Since May 2026 new listings must use the date-versioned OAuth endpoints (e.g. /oauth/2026-03/token) rather than v1, and from 2 Nov 2026 apps on legacy app types or Projects 2023.2/2025.1 are rejected for new listings (v2025.2 or v2026.03 required).
steps.agent_help: Agent drafts the privacy policy section, setup docs, shared-data table and listing copy; you review and submit.

steps.title: HubSpot listing review
steps.detail: Initial review up to 10 business days; the full review and feedback process should take no more than 60 days after feedback is shared. Once listed, installs are unlimited.

requirements.item: HubSpot developer account + HubSpot CLI v7.6.0+
requirements.detail: Apps on the Developer Platform are created and deployed as CLI projects.
At least one; HTTPS required except http://localhost for testing; domain not IP.

requirements.item: Installer is Super Admin or has Marketplace Access
3 active installs, ToS + Privacy Policy URLs, support contact, setup docs
requirements.detail: Marketplace listing prerequisites; listing lifts the 25-install cap.

scopes.purpose: Basic scope required for OAuth; added by default.

scopes.review_impact: No OAuth review; token grants app scopes regardless of the installing user's own record permissions. Must be used if requested, for listing.

scopes.purpose: Companies, deals, tickets and owner assignment.
scopes.review_impact: No review; put rarely-needed ones in optionalScopes.
Enterprise accounts only (tickets: all accounts). As required scopes they make installs fail on lower tiers, so use optionalScopes.

oauth.pkce: Not documented on HubSpot's OAuth pages (unknown).
oauth.refresh_tokens: Access tokens expire after 30 minutes (expires_in 1800). Refresh tokens are long-lived; HubSpot's Jan 2026 blog says they 'don't expire (for now)' unless the app is uninstalled or the token revoked. Whether refresh rotates the refresh token is not documented. Use a lock to avoid concurrent refreshes. The v1 token API is fully deprecated on 16 Feb 2027.
oauth.redirect_uri_rules: Configured in app-hsmeta.json auth.redirectUrls (at least one). HTTPS required in production; http allowed only for localhost; IP addresses not supported. redirect_uri must be sent to authorize and to the token exchange.

limits.limit: 25 installs (excluding developer test accounts) for marketplace-distribution apps
limits.applies_when: Before Marketplace listing; apps created on or migrated to Developer Platform 2025.2+ (enforced 22 Sep 2025)
limits.how_to_lift: Get the app listed on the HubSpot Marketplace.

limits.limit: 10 accounts for private-distribution OAuth apps (100 from a Solutions Partner portal); 1 account for static auth
limits.how_to_lift: Switch to marketplace distribution and list.

limits.limit: 110 requests per 10 seconds per installing account
limits.applies_when: Marketplace-distributed OAuth apps; CRM Search API excluded and has its own stricter limits
limits.how_to_lift: Not raised by the API limit increase add-on; batch and back off.

blockers.symptom: New customers can't install once 25 accounts have the app (unlisted).
blockers.fix: List on the Marketplace (needs 3 active installs), or route overflow customers through Composio managed auth after confirming with Composio that its HubSpot app is not itself capped.

blockers.blocker: Required scope unavailable in customer's tier
blockers.symptom: Authorization page shows an error; users whose account lacks a required scope can't install.
blockers.fix: Move tier-gated scopes (sensitive, custom objects) to optionalScopes and check granted scopes on the token.
Have a Super Admin or user with Marketplace Access install.

blockers.symptom: 401s every ~30 minutes; invalid_grant 'refresh token is invalid, expired or revoked' after uninstall or revoke
blockers.fix: Refresh proactively behind a distributed lock; on invalid_grant, prompt reconnect.

agent_can: Install the HubSpot CLI, scaffold the project and write app-hsmeta.json (distribution, auth, scopes, redirect URLs)
Run hs project upload and fix build errors
Write Composio session code and lock-guarded refresh against the dated token endpoint
Draft privacy policy/ToS sections, setup docs, shared-data table and listing copy
you_must: Log in for hs account auth and create developer test accounts
Copy the client secret into Composio
Install the app (as Super Admin) in your test account
Recruit 3 active unaffiliated installs and submit the Marketplace listing

uncertain: Whether Composio's managed HubSpot app is listed on the HubSpot Marketplace (and so free of the 25-install cap) is not stated in Composio's docs.

Token endpoint versions conflict across HubSpot pages: the working-with-oauth page shows /oauth/v3/token, the deprecation changelog names /oauth/2026-03/token as the replacement, and the current reference uses /oauth/2026-09/token. We list 2026-09 (newest reference); whichever endpoint Composio uses is what matters for a Composio-backed app.
Refresh-token expiry: HubSpot's blog says they don't expire 'for now'. Whether a refresh returns a rotated refresh token is not documented.

The 'authorize the unverified app' checkbox at install suggests HubSpot shows an unverified-app warning for unlisted apps; when it disappears (listing vs certification) is not documented on the fetched pages.
Whether legacy public apps that were never migrated to the 2025.2+ platform still escape the 25-install cap is implied by the changelog but not stated outright.

Verified: HubSpot's May 2026 changelog requires the Uninstall App API (DELETE /appinstalls/v3/external-install) only for certification and recertification submissions, not for plain listings. Which OAuth token endpoint (v1 vs date-versioned) Composio's HubSpot integration calls is not documented, which matters if you list an app used through Composio.
The 3-10 week time-to-listing is an estimate. It depends on how quickly you get 3 unaffiliated active installs and on the number of feedback rounds.
The exact Composio redirect URI for the HUBSPOT toolkit (v3 vs legacy v1) should be copied from the dashboard.
